component.name: Asterism
component.summary: Your AI agents, models and tools on one map

description.p: Asterism shows the AI setup on your computer as cards and a map: coding agents with their plan, limits and usage, local LLMs and their models, MCP servers and skills. Connect them by drawing a line, with a preview and Undo.

ul.li: See what each agent still needs, with the command that fixes it
Install local LLMs and download models; they start and stop with their agents
Find MCP servers and skills on your computer or on the web
A health check: what works, what to fix, and what the setup is good for

description.p: On Omarchy, the same app is the AI Agents Map plugin.

A welcome page for a new Asterism: the agents, local LLMs and online providers as cards with their icons, grouped by kind, the ones found on this PC ticked; a click on a card ticks it, one button switches them on. It shows at every start while nothing is switched on. Settings has an About section with the version and a link to the project on GitHub; the health check line stays away while the map is empty. MCP servers show the skills written for them, whether those still match the server's tools, and Update skill rewrites one with a preview and Undo.

Add-ons: every agent and local LLM Asterism understands is now a signed add-on, and a new Set up page switches on the ones installed on this PC with one click. The Add-ons page lists them with search, details and a homepage button, installs more from the signed catalog, takes a dropped .zip or link, and suggests an add-on when a new agent appears. Agents and local LLMs can be installed and removed from their cards, in a terminal inside the window (sudo asks for your password there). Session numbers per project for OpenCode and Hermes too; session titles and the summary by Claude are now the Insights add-on.

Check for updates (Add MCP › On this PC) moves every app that provides an MCP server to its new version in one step, with one preview, backup and Undo, and then tests each updated server. Models moved to the trash in LM Studio leave the map. Help shows LLM Monitor as a small animation in your theme's colours, and the user manual has new screenshots.

A Healthy & Security check on every agent's details page shows what the agent may do without asking you, explains every setting and choice with its risk, changes them with a preview and Undo, and lists what lowers each risk; local LLMs show whether only this PC can reach them. Help shows the disk space of agents, local LLMs and models. Pin boxes on the map, right-click menus with the cards' actions, move models between folders by dragging. The user manual has a new chapter on security.

An ⓘ legend in the header explains every dot, line and mark of the map. Hide puts away the agents and providers you don't use (a provider only while no shown agent uses one of its models); + Available lists them under Hidden with Show again. Terminal tabs above the map and the terminals show which agents are working, running or ended. The scroll bar no longer covers the cards' arrows in a narrow window.

Agents run in the window: Start here or in a terminal window, Stop on the card, and running agents show a green icon in the cards and the new tree sidebar. Agent details show herdr's live state and Claude Code's subagent runs. The map lights up along the lines of agents that are working. The models page follows LM Studio's layout. Back returns to the page you came from, an opened card scrolls fully into view, the install page has bigger buttons, and the health check line shows only when something needs fixing.

Downloads never write through a link someone planted in a shared model folder (the half-finished file is created new or resumed only when it is your own). Settings fit the window: two columns when it is wide, framed choices, shorter explanations.

Claude Code's details: your last 30 days per project (working time, sessions, tokens, lines changed, API value), topics under Claude Code's own session titles, and an optional written summary by Claude from those titles and numbers.
